reason: For the given input the derivation is deterministic: every cycle has io.req.fire = 1 (s1_isIndirect is hard-wired true, enable resets to 1, io.req.ready is 1 after power-on), so usefulCanReset is 0 every cycle, Counter never advances, resetFinish never asserts, resetSet stays at k and needReset stays 1 for an unbounded number of cycles. No other path clears useful bits table-wide: provider/allocation updates are per-entry and require the same io.update.valid that also blocks the sweep, and allocation is itself blocked on entries whose useful bit is set. The required result (resetSet reaches setsPerBank-1 and needReset clears within a bounded number of cycles independent of every-cycle BPU firing) is therefore violated; completion is bounded only by the number of future FTQ-backpressure cycles, which is not a bound at all under the stated load. The default-config sweep needs 128 or 256 such idle cycles per table, and each stall cycle coinciding with an ITTAGE update is also lost.
